16.title: Classic or alternative steak
16.body:
Beef steaks can be premium (classic) or alternative.

A classic steak is a cut from the back or chest of the animal. The chest, sides and back do not take part in the animal's movement, so the meat has no bones and soft fibres. Premium steaks include ribeye, cowboy, filet mignon and striploin. The cut is valued for its shape, rich taste and tenderness.

An alternative steak is a cut taken from the lumbar part of the animal, usually from the shoulder blade, thighs or flank. These cuts have dense muscle fibres — the meat is tougher, with tendons and fat. Cutting requires more effort — it has an irregular shape and is cut along the fibres.

Alternative steaks include blade, flank or machete. They are much cheaper, but the taste is rich when cooked correctly.

If you are afraid of ruining a steak while cooking, choose classic cuts — they are easy to cook and don't need marinating. Alternative steaks take more work. Choose aged grain-fed meat and use a marinade.

A finished steak gets its name from the part of the bull it was made from. Preferences in choosing meat vary. For example, in America they prefer to grill a thick piece of meat with noble streaks of fat — that is the famous marbled beef. In Europe, on the contrary, small and thin steaks from the tenderloin are preferred.

17.title: Steak doneness levels
17.body:
Hi everyone! How many levels of doneness do you know? How do they differ from each other?

As pros, we know the right answer and share useful information with you.

· BLUE — extra rare — heated to 46–49 °C and quickly "sealed" on the grill, raw but not cold;

· RARE — with "blood" (red juice) — undercooked meat (seared outside, red inside) with red juice, heated to 49–55 °C (cooked 2–3 min at 200 °C);

· MEDIUM RARE — lightly done — undercooked meat with bright pink juice, heated to 55–60 °C (cooked 4–5 min at 190–200 °C);

· MEDIUM — medium done meat with light pink juice inside, heated to 60–65 °C (cooked 6–7 min at 180 °C);

· MEDIUM WELL — almost done — meat with clear juice, heated to 65–69 °C (cooked 8–9 min at 180 °C);

· WELL DONE — fully cooked meat with almost no juice, heated to 71–100 °C (cooked 8–9 min at 180 °C and finished in a combi oven);

· TOO WELL DONE, OVERCOOKED — fully cooked meat with no juice at all, heated above 100 °C.

22.title: Cooking the perfect steak at home. Chef's tips
22.body:
Cooking the perfect steak at home. Chef's tips

The right steak is tender, moderately seared, aromatic, juicy and very tasty. Here is a step-by-step guide from our chef Dmitry Pupyshev, from choosing the meat to serving a delicious steak.

🔴 Step 1 – Choosing the meat

Ideally, it's farm meat from a young bull (up to 2 years old), grass- or grain-fed. A grain #diet makes the meat marbled — with thin layers of fat.

The optimal thickness of a piece of meat is 2.5-3.5 cm.

Filet mignon — up to 8 cm.

Which parts to take?

Ribeye — the shoulder part

Porterhouse — the lumbar section

Filet mignon — the round muscle

T-bone — meat with a T-shaped bone

Striploin — boneless fillet from the triangular part of the back.

💡 Any of these steaks can be bought chilled from us at @ugli_ekb.


🔴 Step 2 – Preparation

A warm steak cooks quickly and evenly.

🔻Frozen — leave in the fridge for 8-12 hours, take out 60 minutes before cooking, bring to room temperature, pat dry with a napkin.

🔻Chilled — take out of the fridge 60 minutes before.

⚠️ Important! Don't beat the meat, otherwise it will lose its structure and its juice when frying.

❓ Marinate or not? When to salt and pepper?

We recommend:

Don't marinate steaks unless it's some signature #recipe.

Salt 10-20 minutes BEFORE frying — the piece will be evenly salted. If you salt after frying, you'll get a salty crust with an unsalted middle.

It's better to pepper after frying — that way you get the aroma of fresh pepper, not burnt pepper.

Before putting the steak in the pan, brush it with olive oil.

🔴 Step 3 – Frying

Fry steaks in a well-heated grill pan or just one with a thick bottom. We recommend frying no more than one steak in one pan at a time.



Important! Once you've put the steak in, don't press it down — it will lose its juice and become tougher.

Fry the steaks for 1.5-7 minutes on each side depending on the size and the desired doneness. Then, holding with tongs, sear the edges for 30 seconds on each side.

To Medium, a 3 cm steak is fried for 3-4 minutes on each side. At the end you can add butter (also flavoured with herbs or mushrooms) and rosemary for a golden crust and flavour.


After taking it off the pan, you can finish the steak in an oven preheated to 200°C for 5 minutes. Or leave it on the table on a warm plate for about 10 minutes, covered with foil. During this time the meat "rests" and the juice keeps moving inside, finishing the steak from within.

The steak is ready. Time to serve!

⚠️ But if you're not sure it will turn out, it's important to serve guests a first-class steak, or there's no time to cook and clean the kitchen afterwards — order a great steak at ugli-ekb.ru
